rounds.proof_sketch: With N=4096, BLOCK_SIZE=16: k ∈ {0,16,32,...,4080}, tx ∈ {0,...,15}. Original condition (k+tx)<N: max(k+tx)=4080+15=4095<4096, ALWAYS TRUE. Mutated condition (k-tx)<N: max(k-tx)=4080-0=4080<4096, min(k-tx)=0-15=-15<4096, ALWAYS TRUE. Both predicates evaluate identically (true) for all valid thread/loop iterations.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the bounds-checking condition from (k+tx)<N to (k-tx)<N in the tile-loading logic. For the fixed matrix size N=4096 with BLOCK_SIZE=16, the loop variable k takes values {0,16,32,...,4080} and thread index tx ranges [0,15]. The original condition (k+tx)<4096 is always satisfied because max(k+tx)=4095<4096. The mutated condition (k-tx)<4096 is also always satisfied because the maximum value k-tx=4080 and minimum k-tx=-15, both less than 4096. Since both predicates are perpetually true, the else-branch (setting tile_A to 0) is never reached in either version, making them behaviorally identical.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation would cause different behavior only for matrix sizes where N is not perfectly divisible by BLOCK_SIZE (e.g., N=4097), or where N < BLOCK_SIZE. With N=4096 and BLOCK_SIZE=16, both bounds-check conditions are always true, so no value-level test can distinguish them.
rounds.recommendations: For comprehensive mutation testing of tiled GPU kernels, the test suite should include non-tile-aligned dimensions (e.g., N=4097, N=17) to expose bounds-checking mutations. Under fixed-shape contracts where dimensions happen to align perfectly with tile sizes, arithmetic mutations to bounds predicates become semantically equivalent and undetectable.
